title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 4 close: Lyranus — mark of destined vessels, not foresight-cause
pass_a_gloss: Thus Lyranus seems to have understood this place, who explains these words, he shall be a vessel unto honour, that is, he shall be a vessel applied to Divine worship. But in whatever way this place be understood, it does not prove that God elects us unto glory from foresight of our sanctity, but that those elect unto glory are imbued with true sanctity, and by this mark are recognized as vessels destined unto honour, and are actually applied to honourable use through this sanctity.
pass_b_english: So Lyranus seems to take the place: "he will be a vessel unto honour" means a vessel set apart for divine worship. However you read it, the text does not prove God elects us to glory from foresight of our holiness. It proves the elect to glory are filled with true holiness, known by that mark as vessels destined to honour, and actually put to honourable use through that holiness.
source_text: Sic videtur hunc locum intellexisse Lyranus, qui exponit haec verba, erit vas in honorem id est, erit vas Divino cultui applicatum. Sed quocunque modo intelligatur hic locus, non probat Deum nos eligere ad gloriam ex praevisione nostrae sanctitatis, sed electos ad gloriam imbui vera sanctitate, & ex hac nota pro vasis ad honorem destinatis agnosci, & actualiter ad usum honorabilem per hanc sanctitatem applicari.
